problems.description: 87 convention violations (convention score 0.57) concentrated in index.ts, exampleLoggerPlugin.ts, and cache.ts: classes and interfaces not PascalCase, constants not UPPER_CASE, and functions using snake_case — a Python idiom leaking into TypeScript. This is a systematic naming style failure, not an isolated slip.

SonarQube reports 4 code smells and +24 cognitive complexity across only 7 new functions (~3.4 complexity/fn average) in a greenfield scaffold — convoluted control flow and over-wrapping in code that should be straightforward.

package-lock.json resolves very new @babel/* 7.29.x and picocolors 1.1.x dependencies while the project declares no engines field, so there is no version guard tying the toolchain (jest 29, ts-jest) to a supported Node runtime.

strengths: Sensible greenfield structure: jest + ts-jest preset, typed bin entry (dist/cli.js), and src/tests root split match the standard TypeScript Node project layout.
Appropriate dependency selection for a static site generator (commander for CLI, gray-matter for frontmatter, marked for markdown) with no runtime bloat.
0 bugs, 0 duplications, and a 15-file/24-import modular split rather than a monolith — the architecture itself is sound.
commit_reviews.summary: The architecture is a reasonable SSG scaffold, but it ships with a systematic naming-convention failure (87 violations, snake_case in TS) and elevated cognitive complexity, making this a poor-quality foundation for the story.

problems.description: No test files appear in the diff for the new TemplateEngine (93-line module with layout caching, partial loading, and dual render paths). The engine- vs built-in-fallback rendering is the core new logic and is left unverified.

SonarQube delta shows +17 cognitive complexity and +1 smell. The dual-path pattern `engine?.renderPage(page, pages) ?? renderPage(page)` in generator.ts:68 duplicates the rendering pipeline, and the CLI's `--templates` default of './templates' makes feature activation implicit (only kicks in when the dir exists) rather than an explicit flag.

FLAGGED DISCREPANCY: mechanical convention score is 0.57 (87 violations), but the cited violations (PascalCase classes/interfaces, UPPER_CASE constants, snake_case functions) are in exampleLoggerPlugin.ts and cache.ts — files not touched by this diff. The score appears to reflect cumulative pre-existing worktree state, not this commit; the new code itself uses compliant PascalCase class, camelCase functions, and UPPER_CASE constants.

strengths: Backward-compatible optional integration: built-in renderers remain the fallback when no templates directory exists, so the feature is non-breaking.
Clean module separation — TemplateEngine is isolated in its own file and exported consistently through index.ts like the other modules.
Reuses existing body renderers (renderArticleBody/renderIndexBody) instead of duplicating rendering logic, respecting the existing codebase structure.
Consistent dependency management: package.json and package-lock.json agree, and handlebars is correctly promoted out of devDependencies in the lockfile.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-integrated, backward-compatible template-engine feature that respects existing patterns and reuses prior renderers, though it ships without tests and with mildly elevated cognitive complexity — while the poor mechanical convention score appears to stem from pre-existing files outside this diff.

problems.description: The serve command's async action has no try/catch around startDevServer — a port-in-use or EADDRINUSE error surfaces as an unhandled rejection instead of a clean CLI error, and parseInt(opts.port, 10) is unvalidated (NaN silently accepted).

The new devServer module ships with no tests; only the pure, exported injectLiveReload is trivially testable, leaving the static file server and live-reload wiring unverified despite a +14 import / +5 function surface.
Cognitive complexity +24 concentrates in serveStaticFile's nested traversal-guard / MIME / directory-rewrite branches; extractable but not yet a smell, and not introduced as debt.

strengths: Feature fits the existing architecture: a new commander subcommand mirrors the build command's option/default/resolve pattern exactly
Reuses buildSite from ./generator rather than duplicating build logic, and extends BuildOptions for the new port option
Exports a pure, injectable injectLiveReload function and keeps DevServerOptions/DevServer as typed interfaces — good separation and testability
Defense-in-depth on static serving: path traversal guard and MIME-type map present, plus proper @types/ws dev dependency
commit_reviews.summary: A cohesive, convention-clean dev-server feature that slots cleanly into the existing CLI architecture (better); the 0.57 convention score and 87 violations cited are all in untouched files (index.ts, exampleLoggerPlugin.ts, cache.ts), so they reflect the codebase baseline, not this diff — the new code itself adheres to PascalCase/camelCase conventions.

problems.description: Incremental build bypasses the established plugin pipeline (ssg.ts/plugin.ts). buildSiteIncremental re-implements page/index rendering via direct parseMarkdown/TemplateEngine/renderIndex calls and is explicitly incompatible with --config/plugins, creating two divergent build paths that will drift as the normal path evolves.

Duplicated rendering logic: the incremental path mirrors what buildSite already does through plugins instead of reusing it, so fixes to rendering must be applied in two places. SonarQube cognitive complexity +47 and +1 smell corroborate the branching/duplication cost.

New modules use namespace imports (import * as fs/path/crypto) and the synchronous fs API (readFileSync/writeFileSync/mkdirSync) while the existing codebase uses node:-prefixed default imports and async fs/promises throughout; the sync calls also block the event loop in an otherwise async CLI.

Measured convention violations in cache.ts (snake_case functions) and repo-wide (0.57 score, 87 findings including index.ts/exampleLoggerPlugin.ts PascalCase/UPPER_CASE issues). Note: the diffed cache.ts uses camelCase, so part of the measured violation set appears to be pre-existing repo state rather than introduced by this commit.
No tests added for the new cache/incremental modules; the -2 bug delta (SonarQube bugs +2) and new sync-I/O paths have no coverage guarding cache load/save or stale-detection edge cases.

strengths: Cache module is well-isolated and well-documented, with versioned manifests and uniform fallback handling for missing, corrupt, or version-mismatched cache files.
Template-directory-level invalidation with rationale is sound — correctly avoids unsafe per-file invalidation for shared partials/layouts.
Good UX escape hatches: --clean forces full rebuild, and combining --incremental with --config degrades gracefully with a warning instead of silently misbehaving.
commit_reviews.summary: This is a functional but architecturally divergent cross-cutting change: it adds a cleanly-documented cache layer, yet implements incremental builds as a plugin-bypassing, synchronous parallel path that duplicates rendering logic and introduces technical debt, while the measured convention score (0.57) largely reflects pre-existing repo findings rather than new violations.

compounding_issues: Seed mismatch: the provided seed was an unrelated Express/JWT auth API, so Session 1 rebuilt an SSG greenfield and never deleted the orphaned root index.ts — dead code that lingers through all five sessions

Session 2 committed a hand-rolled regex-based Handlebars/EJS template engine whose 2 new tests failed at commit time (test setup never mkdir'd the content dir; ENOENT) and stayed red through Session 3

Session 4's plugin refactor introduced 8 TypeScript type errors (MarkdownPlugin fails structural Plugin typing, plugin-array union mismatches, onFile missing on union) breaking tsc and the entire Jest suite (0 tests run) in Sessions 4-5

Ambiguous module layout after the refactor: root plugins/*.ts shims + src/plugins/*.ts + src/server.ts re-exports all coexist under rootDir '.', and DevServerPlugin is an empty placeholder class that nominally satisfies the new Plugin interface
Session 5 layered incremental caching onto the already-broken Session 4 base without restoring a green compile or test run, so the story ends with a non-compiling, untestable codebase
key_decisions: Session 1: built the static site generator greenfield instead of reusing the mismatched auth-API seed — right call for the story, but the 200-line seed file was never removed

Session 2: hand-rolled a dual-engine template system (Handlebars-style and EJS-style with layouts/partials) using string regex plus Function('context', ...) rather than adding handlebars/ejs dependencies
Session 3: added a chokidar + ws live-reload dev server exposed via a 'serve' CLI subcommand, integrating the build core into a serving pipeline

Session 4: refactored to a plugin architecture (Plugin interface, BuildContext, onStart/beforeBuild/afterBuild/onFile/onEnd hooks) extracting markdown, template, and dev-server into plugins — the most consequential architectural choice, but the types were left broken
Session 5: added incremental builds with SHA-256 content hashing, template-hash invalidation, and a versioned .ssg-cache.json manifest threaded through BuildContext
story_review.trajectory_description: The ambition curve rises while the build-health curve falls. Session 1 is a clean, well-structured core that compiles and passes 2/2 tests. Session 2 lands a substantial templating feature but commits with 2 failing tests (untested at commit). Session 3 adds the dev server on top of those same red tests. Session 4 makes the boldest architectural move — the plugin system — but breaks type-checking outright, collapsing the entire Jest suite to 0 runnable tests. Session 5 then extends the cache system on that broken base, never restoring a compiling tree or a passing test. Functionality and architectural sophistication clearly increase across the arc, but verification discipline degrades monotonically after Session 1, leaving the final product more capable yet mechanically broken.
story_review.summary: A thematically coherent five-session SSG arc (core → templating → dev server → plugin architecture → incremental caching) whose quality declined in discipline terms, ending with a sophisticated codebase that fails to compile and cannot run its own tests.
